name: transaction_links
description: A pre-funded link a member hands to someone else, who redeems it. The amount is held until it is redeemed or expires.

columns.name: hold_available_amount_gdd4
columns.description: The part of the sender's balance withheld while the link is outstanding, so it cannot be spent twice.

columns.name: code
columns.description: The redemption code carried in the link. Whoever holds it can redeem — treat it as a bearer secret.

columns.name: deleted_at
columns.description: Soft delete: the sender withdrew the link before it was redeemed.

indexes.name: idx_userId
indexes.note: Redundant with the leading column of idx_user_id_valid_until. Do not recreate it in gradido2.

notes: Legacy names these columns in camelCase — userId, validUntil, redeemedBy — unlike every other table, and the migrations confirm it (idx_user_id_valid_until ON transaction_links(userId, validUntil, id)). gradido2 uses snake_case as its own rule requires; legacyName records what to read from a legacy database during migration.

The three states are distinguished by columns, not by a status enum: outstanding (redeemed_at and deleted_at null, valid_until in the future), redeemed (redeemed_at set), expired (valid_until passed), withdrawn (deleted_at set). Both implementations must derive the state the same way — an expired link that was also withdrawn is withdrawn.
code is a bearer secret: never logged, never returned for a link the caller does not own. See logging.json.

Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. Legacy declares these as datetime without the precision(3) the other tables use — second precision. Verify before relying on sub-second ordering.
